DEFENSIVES LEADCyclicals -6.7% vs defensives on the month
Rotation ReadCitrini · claude

The rotation is defensive and it is accelerating. Every cyclical bucket is bleeding while consumer staples (XLP +2.75% in a month, +16.33% YTD) and utilities (XLU +1.81% this month) sit in the top of the board. The worst of the selling is concentrated in the highest-beta growth themes: software -22.9%, quantum -29.1%, AI infra -17.9%, semis -16.3%. That is a de-risking, and it is happening inside a market where energy still shows +31.15% YTD even after -14.03% in a month. The winners of the year are being sold to fund the safety of staples. That is the tell you should trade against if you think the year ends hot. You should not. The month says otherwise.

The central tension is cyclical collapse against defensive bid, and breadth has broken down alongside it. Consumer discretionary (XLY +2.34% this month) is holding up only because it is being dragged by staples' coattails, not by any industrial or materials leadership. The cyclical sectors are rolling: XLK -12.85%, XLE -14.03%, XLI -2.69%, XLB -2.88%. Meanwhile the ratio of industrials to staples (XLI/XLP) sits at a z-score of -2.51, in the bottom 2% of its yearly range, confirming that the sector rotation is not noise. The most stretched ratios tell you where the pain is most acute: GDXJ/GDX at -3.41, XME/XLB at -2.69, all in the bottom 1% of their yearly ranges. These are not just mean-reversion candidates. They are the fingerprints of a market that has already priced a hard landing in cyclical assets. The second-order implication is clear: if you are long cyclicals, you are betting on a reversal that the ratio data says is not yet in motion. The one data point that flips this read is XLI/XLP recovering above its 2% floor, meaning industrials start outperforming staples again. Until that happens, the defensive trade has the momentum and the math.

The extremes in relative strength cut both ways and you should handle them separately. The bottom-of-range ratios in cyclical versus defensive pairs (XLI/XLP at -2.51, XLB/XLP at -2.35, both in the bottom 2% of their yearly ranges) are mean-reversion candidates in a vacuum, but the breadth of the selling in the underlying sectors suggests they are confirming trend, not exhausting it. Do not fade these yet. The top-of-range ratios are the real reversion setup: GLD/SLV at +2.57 in the top 100% of its yearly range, TLT/GLD at +2.49 in the top 100%, and BKLN/HYG at +2.34 in the top 98%. These are stretched to the upside, meaning the haven bid and the credit-quality bid are extreme. If any of these ratios begins to roll over, that is your signal that risk appetite is returning. The other side is the GDXJ/GDX ratio at -3.41 in the bottom 1% of its range, which is a pure small-cap miner versus large-cap miner spread. That is a liquidity trade, not a macro trade, and it will snap back violently if the broad market stabilizes. Watch the GLD/TLT ratio at -2.21 in the bottom 1% of its range: gold underperforming long bonds is a classic risk-off signature, and it is sitting at an extreme that historically precedes a reversal. If that ratio starts moving up, it means the haven trade is unwinding and you should rotate back toward cyclical exposure.

Defensive sectors and themes are leading while cyclical and growth exposures are collapsing across the board.

BULL

The year-to-date leaders in energy (+31.15%) and biotech (+35.6%) are still positive on the year, and consumer discretionary (+2.34%) is holding up. A rotation back into these groups is possible if the haven bid fades. The bottom-of-range cyclical ratios like XLI/XLP at -2.51 are stretched enough to snap back.

BEAR

The monthly performance is decisively risk-off: software -22.9%, quantum -29.1%, AI infra -17.9%. The defensive sectors are the only ones with positive momentum. The top-of-range haven ratios like GLD/SLV at +2.57 and TLT/GLD at +2.49 confirm that capital is flowing to safety.

TELL

The XLI/XLP ratio at -2.51 (bottom 2% of its yearly range) or a rollover in GLD/SLV at +2.57 (top 100% of its range) will resolve the tension. If either reverses, the defensive trade is done.

The monthly performance shows the rotation is happening now, and defensives are winning. Trust the monthly data over YTD; the defensive bid is the active trend.
⚠ The XLI/XLP ratio at -2.51 in the bottom 2% of its yearly range suggests cyclicals are due for mean reversion. vs XLI is down 2.69% this month while XLP is up 2.75%, showing cyclicals are still losing ground.: A low ratio does not mean it cannot go lower. The momentum is still negative for cyclicals. Trust the momentum, not the stretched ratio, until XLI/XLP shows any upward inflection.

The most extreme readings in relative strength are pointing to two different regimes. The bottom-of-range ratios (GDXJ/GDX at -3.41, XME/XLB at -2.69, XLI/XLP at -2.51, XLB/XLP at -2.35, all in the bottom 2% or lower of their yearly ranges) look like classic mean-reversion candidates, but you should not fade them.

The breadth of the selling in the underlying cyclical sectors (XLI -2.69%, XLB -2.88%, XLK -12.85%) says the trend is still down. These extremes are confirming the trend.

The top-of-range ratios are where the real reversions will come from: GLD/SLV at +2.57 in the top 100% of its yearly range, TLT/GLD at +2.49 in the top 100%, and BKLN/HYG at +2.34 in the top 98%. These are the haven and credit-quality bids that have run to extremes.

When they start to crack, that is the signal the risk-off rotation is exhausting. Watch GLD/TLT at -2.21 (bottom 1% of its range) as the swing factor.

If gold starts outperforming long bonds again, the haven trade is unwinding and you should rotate back into risk.
